stand: South Korea and the US-led UN Command have concluded North Korea planted the anti-personnel mines that wounded three soldiers in the DMZ on 21 September. Seoul (Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul, spokeswoman Chung Bin-na) demands an apology, is weighing further measures, and has begun clearing mines south of the Military Demarcation Line. Pyongyang, through Kim Yo Jong, denies its soldiers crossed the line and rejected a proposal to resurvey the border. North Korea's Foreign Ministry has warned of retaliatory force against any Southern incursion.

timeline.text: Two mines exploded in the DMZ, injuring three South Korean soldiers, two seriously.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff gave a preliminary assessment blaming North Korean mines.
Kim Yo Jong denied North Korean soldiers crossed the border, calling the incident a farce.
Unification Minister Chung Dong-young proposed a joint resurvey of the MDL.
Kim Yo Jong rejected the resurvey proposal, saying the border will be set by force.
South Korea's military announced final investigation results naming North Korea responsible and demanded an apology.
South Korea's military carried out a mine-clearing operation at the blast site.
North Korea's Foreign Ministry warned it would use force against any Southern military incursion.
Seoul said it was not ruling out measures to force an apology from Pyongyang.
